title: Address Poisoning & Vanity Vanity Zero-Value Transfer Exploits
summary: Mechanics of zero-value token transfer spam generating fake transaction history with vanity addresses matching victims' first and last characters.
content: Address poisoning is an evasion and deception tactic where attackers generate vanity addresses that share the same leading 4-6 characters and trailing 4-6 characters as a victim's frequent counterparty. The scammer triggers a 0-value ERC-20 Transfer event (often abusing poorly implemented token contracts or executing valid 0-value transfers) from or to the victim's address. When the victim subsequently copies an address from their wallet transaction history without checking the entire 42-character hex string, funds are mistakenly routed to the attacker. In graph analysis, poisoned addresses exhibit high incoming 0-value transfer fan-out with minimal to zero subsequent native gas expenditure.
